Node 26: released 2026-05-05; scheduled LTS date 2026-10-28; Maintenance 2027-10-20; EOL 2029-04-30. As of 2026-10-17 it is NOT yet LTS (still Current); LTS begins in 11 days per schedule. previous-releases page lists v26 as 'Current'.
Node 22: start 2024-04-24; Active LTS 2024-10-29; Maintenance 2025-10-21; EOL 2027-04-30. As of 2026-10-17 it is Maintenance LTS (supported, critical fixes/security only), not EOL.

Recommendation for a deployment requiring LTS today (2026-10-17): choose Node 24. It is Active LTS now and supported to 2028-04-30. Node 26 is not LTS until 2026-10-28; reconsider migrating to 26 after that date, once its LTS release is actually published and your dependencies are tested.

**Schedule text from the page:**
- Major versions are in *Current* status for six months, giving library authors time to add support.
- Historically (up to Node.js 26), odd-numbered releases become unsupported after six months, and even-numbered releases move to *Active LTS* and are ready for general use.
- Starting with Node.js 27, the release cycle becomes annual. Each major version moves to *LTS* after its six-month *Current* phase, following six additional months of *Alpha* phase.
- LTS typically guarantees critical bug fixes for a total of 30 months.
- Production applications should only use *Active LTS* or *Maintenance LTS* releases.
- Full schedule details are on GitHub: https://github.com/nodejs/release#release-schedule
